from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines_text = [
            "Which path minimizes the time between these points?",
            "Gravity pulls objects down a wire path.",
            "Compare three paths: straight, arc, and curve.",
            "Which bead reaches the end first?",
            "The answer is not a straight line."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Race of Gravity", lecture_lines_text)
        
        # Define paths
        start = self.grid["B1"]
        end = self.grid["E6"]
        
        straight_path = Line(start, end, color=WHITE)
        arc_path = ArcBetweenPoints(start, end, angle=-TAU/8, color=WHITE)
        curve_path = CubicBezier(
            start, 
            start + np.array([1, 1, 0]), 
            end + np.array([-1, 1, 0]), 
            end, 
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        bead1 = Dot(start, color="#FFD700")
        bead2 = Dot(start, color="#FFD700")
        bead3 = Dot(start, color="#FFD700")
        
        self.add(straight_path, arc_path, curve_path, bead1, bead2, bead3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Show gravity concept
        gravity_arrow = Arrow(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(gravity_arrow, "C1")
        self.play(Create(gravity_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(straight_path), FadeIn(arc_path), FadeIn(curve_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Racing beads
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(bead1, straight_path, run_time=3, rate_func=linear),
            MoveAlongPath(bead2, arc_path, run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear),
            MoveAlongPath(bead3, curve_path, run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(Indicate(curve_path, color="#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Brachistochrone means the shortest time path.",
            "Straight lines are short, but slow.",
            "Curves allow faster speeds early on.",
            "Gravity rewards a steep initial drop.",
            "The curve balances distance and speed."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Brachistochrone", lecture_lines)

        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20).next_to(dot_b, RIGHT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pts))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        line = Line(dot_a.get_center(), dot_b.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        curve = ArcBetweenPoints(dot_a.get_center(), dot_b.get_center(), angle=-TAU/6, color=RED)
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"T = \int \frac{ds}{v}", color=WHITE)

        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        v_var = formula[0][6]

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Solution: The Cycloid", [
            "The solution path is a cycloid.",
            "A cycloid traces a point on a rolling circle.",
            "It is defined by parametric equations.",
            "X equals r times theta minus sine theta.",
            "Y equals r times one minus cosine theta."
        ])

        eq = MathTex(r"x = r(\theta - \sin \theta)", r"\\", r"y = r(1 - \cos \theta)", font_size=32)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
        point = Dot(color=RED)
        point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circle.get_center() + np.array([0, -0.5, 0])))
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(circle, point), "C2")
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(point))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.place_in_area(eq, "A3", "B5")
        self.play(Write(eq))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Conclusion", [
            "Nature optimizes descent for the fastest time.", 
            "Hawks dive using a similar cycloid shape.", 
            "Optimal angles maximize high-speed performance."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a cycloid curve (Nature optimizes)
        cycloid = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t - np.sin(t), -1 + np.cos(t), 0]),
            t_range=[0, 2*PI],
            color="#00FF00"
        )
        self.place_in_area(cycloid, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(cycloid))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent the hawk's path (cycloid shape)
        hawk_path = cycloid.copy().set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(FadeIn(hawk_path))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Summarize (Brachistochrone and Tautochrone)
        summary = Text("Optimal Path: Cycloid", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(summary, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(summary))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Curve of Fastest Descent

sections.title: The Hook: The Race of Gravity
sections.content: Introduce the challenge: A bead slides down a wire from point A to point B under gravity. We compare three paths: a straight line, a circular arc, and a curve. Ask students to intuit which shape wins the race.
sections.example: Visual: A split-screen animation showing three beads racing; the 'straight line' beads finish slower than the one on the mysterious curved path.

sections.title: Prerequisite Concept: Conservation of Energy
sections.content: Briefly review the Work-Energy Theorem. Explain that gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy (v = sqrt(2gh)). The path determines the speed profile at every point.
sections.example: Visual: A schematic showing a ball at height h gaining velocity as it descends, emphasizing that 'dropping' early increases speed for later stages.

sections.title: Defining the Brachistochrone
sections.content: Define 'Brachistochrone' (Greek: shortest time). Explain that the path is not the shortest distance (straight line), but the one that maximizes velocity early on by dipping lower.
sections.example: Visual: A plot showing how the straight line is too slow initially, while the cycloid path drops steeply to gain velocity before leveling out.

sections.title: The Mathematical Solution: The Cycloid
sections.content: Introduce the Cycloid—the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling circle. Present the parametric equations x = r(θ - sinθ) and y = r(1 - cosθ). Connect this geometry to the physical optimization.
sections.example: Visual: An animation of a red circle rolling along a ceiling, with a single point tracing out the path (the cycloid) between point A and B.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize that the shortest time is achieved by a curve that balances distance and velocity. Mention its occurrence in nature, such as a hawk diving for prey at an optimal angle.
sections.example: Visual: A video clip of a falcon in a 'stoop' (high-speed dive), visually overlaying a cycloid curve to show how nature optimizes the path for the fastest descent.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The gravity arrow at C1 is positioned too close to the left-side lecture text, creating visual clutter and potential obstruction. Fix: self.place_at_grid(gravity_arrow, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=6, object=gravity_arrow)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The race path graphic overlaps with the center-right grid area, reducing the visual separation between the concept and the structural layout. Fix: self.place_in_area(race_path_graphic, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=10, object=race_path_graphic)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The 'Grid Visual' title is positioned too high, leaving significant unused whitespace in the lower half while crowding the top border. Fix: self.place_at_grid(grid_title, 'A4', scale_factor=1.0) (line=0, object=grid_title)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Formulas are crowded vertically and lack balance, with scale too large for the 6x6 grid container. Fix: Line 61: self.place_at_grid(u_formula, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=61, object=u_formula)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The second formula overlaps the vertical proximity of the first, creating visual tension. Fix: Line 62: self.place_at_grid(k_formula, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=62, object=k_formula)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The final formula is positioned too low, leading to poor visual equilibrium. Fix: Line 63: self.place_at_grid(total_formula, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=63, object=total_formula)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The Brachistochrone curve and formula obstruct the right-side visual space, potentially conflicting with the grid layout. Fix: Line 3: self.place_in_area(brachistochrone_curve, 'A3', 'D6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=3, object=brachistochrone_curve)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The integral formula is centered on C2, which is too close to the lecture area, creating visual clutter. Fix: Line 4: self.place_at_grid(formula, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0) (line=4, object=formula)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Points A and B are inconsistently positioned, causing visual imbalance with the grid structure. Fix: Line 5: self.place_at_grid(point_A, 'A4', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_at_grid(point_B, 'F5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=5, object=points_A_B)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The equation is positioned too far to the right, creating visual imbalance and wasting grid space. Fix: self.place_in_area(eq, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9) (line=4, object=eq)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The rolling circle animation overlaps with the horizontal reach of the equation, causing visual clutter. Fix: self.place_at_grid(circle, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=2, object=circle)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The red point label is not clearly associated with the circle's position due to current proximity. Fix: self.place_at_grid(point_label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5) (line=2, object=point_label)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Cycloid curve occupies too much horizontal space, crowding the center and risking collision with the lecture text area. Fix: Line 62: self.place_in_area(cycloid, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.5) (line=62, object=cycloid)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The summary label 'Optimal Path: Cycloid' is poorly aligned and sits too low, creating visual imbalance. Fix: Line 77: self.place_at_grid(summary, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=77, object=summary)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The grid utilization is off-center, leaving excessive whitespace in the upper right quadrant. Fix: Shift assets toward the bottom right quadrant to maintain left-side negative space for lecture text readability. (line=0, object=all)
